arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Timbs' counsel argued the freedom from excessive fines applies to states.
Indiana's counsel argued in rem forfeitures have long existed without proportionality limits.
Justice Ginsburg questioned if this logic excludes non-citizens from protections.
Justice Alito asked if a six-year prison sentence would violate the Eighth Amendment.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Timbs seeks a federal limit on state property seizures. Indiana defends its right to seize property without federal constraints.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Timbs wants the federal Constitution to limit state property seizures.
Indiana wants to keep its power to seize property without federal limits.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Timbs argues the Eighth Amendment applies to states through the Fourteenth Amendment.
Indiana argues the Eighth Amendment does not restrict state property seizures.
